description:
Return ONE filing already parsed for you: its available normalised text and its tables as structured cells. Call it after list_company_filings, with the `aann_` id that tool returned, when you need what a filing actually says rather than just its title and PDF link.

This is the step your own pipeline would otherwise have to do: a filing PDF is a layout format, not a data format, so pulling clean text and real table cells out of it is where ad-hoc extraction usually goes wrong. Tables come back as rows of cells you can read directly, not as an image or a flattened blob.

It serves ONE filing per call, whose date is at most seven days before the database current date (eight calendar dates including today). Older filings are not gone — the filing itself and its source PDF link stay available from list_company_filings for the company's whole history; only the parsed text is recent-only. When that is why you got nothing, `reason` says outside_parsed_window, which is a different answer from unknown_filing.

Source coverage is limited: PDFs over 150 pages are parsed only through the first 30 pages; table coverage is limited above 50 pages. Use source links for the complete original. text_chars measures stored text, not source completeness. text_truncated=false or next_text_offset=null does not mean every PDF page was parsed.

Stored text arrives in slices: read `text_chars` for the stored total and call again with `next_text_offset` until it is null. Do NOT use this to sweep a company or the market — it takes a single filing id and has no cursor.

Read `text_unavailable` before trusting the text. Two of its values are properties of the source file — a scan with no text layer, or a font we cannot map to Unicode — and retrying those will not help. A third, parse_failed, means the failure is ours rather than the document's, and asking again later may well work. Either way the source links are still worth opening.

aann_.description: Opaque filing id from list_company_filings, e.g. aann_Kyw46MM1gCnIaBxA.
aann_.title: Aann

text_offset.description: 0-based offset into the filing's full text. Start at 0; then pass next_text_offset from the previous call.
text_offset.title: Text Offset

name: get_filing_parsed

outputSchema.description: One filing's parsed text and tables (tier 2).

found.description: False means either we hold no filing under this id, or the filing is outside the parsed-text window. Read `reason` to tell those apart.
found.title: Found

next_text_offset.description: Where to continue, or null at the end of stored text, not necessarily the source PDF.
next_text_offset.title: Next Text Offset

reason.description: unknown_filing = no such filing id. outside_parsed_window = the filing exists and its source PDF is still available from list_company_filings, but parsed text is only served for recent filings.
reason.title: Reason

sources.description: Every source link we hold for this filing, best first. Use them to check our text against the original.
sources.title: Sources

tables.description: Tables as cells, in document order: {index, page, n_rows, n_cols, cells, continuation_of}. continuation_of points at the table this one continues from when a table spans pages. Empty list means this filing has no tables.
tables.title: Tables

text.description: Normalised plain text of this filing, from `text_offset`, at most `limits.parsed_text_chunk_chars` characters per call.
text.title: Text

text_chars.description: Length of stored parsed text, which may cover only part of the PDF. Compare with text_offset + len(text) to see how much is left.
text_chars.title: Text Chars

text_truncated.description: True when more stored text follows. False does not guarantee full PDF coverage.
text_truncated.title: Text Truncated

text_unavailable.description: Why the text cannot be used, or null when it can. no_text_layer = the source PDF carries no text layer at all (a scan), so there is nothing to extract. unreadable_font_encoding = it has text, but the PDF embeds a subset font without a Unicode map, so the characters come out as (cid:NNNN) placeholders; the text is still returned, and the numbers and structure may still be readable, but the words are not. Those two are properties of the source file — re-requesting will not help. parse_failed means the failure is OURS, not the document's: we did not parse it successfully, and it is worth asking again later. Check this field rather than testing whether `text` is empty.
text_unavailable.title: Text Unavailable

window_days.description: Maximum filing-date age in database calendar days, inclusive of age zero.
window_days.title: Window Days

outputSchema.title: ParsedFilingResult
